component.name: Kalipso
component.summary: Teleprompter that follows your voice, on your device

description.p: Keep your script next to your camera and read naturally. Kalipso is one window: large, you write your script in it with bold, italic, sections and cues; small, under the camera, it shows the next words and dims the ones you have already read.

ul.li: Follow your voice with local speech recognition, scroll at a steady speed, or step with the keyboard, a foot pedal or your phone.
Scripts and reading positions are saved automatically on your device.
Bracketed cues are shown but never read aloud; headings become sections you can jump to.
Import speaker notes from PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress presentations.
Mirror the text for beam-splitter teleprompter glass.

description.p: Speech recognition runs on this device. Kalipso downloads the voice model for your language once, from its Settings.
On GNOME, Settings turns on Kalipso's top bar reader.
On Windows, upgrading with the installer no longer leaves Kalipso unable to start.
On Debian and Ubuntu, check boxes and drop-down lists show their marks again outside KDE.
Voice commands are removed: words you say only ever follow the script.
The selected script in the scripts panel keeps the reader's colours on light desktops.

ul.li: One window that writes and reads, with text size buttons and a scripts panel.
Voice following on this device in Italian and five more languages, steady speed (150 words a minute to begin with) or manual steps.
A Plasma widget and a GNOME Shell extension that read the app's scripts.
Packages for Arch, Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora, a Windows installer and a macOS disk image.
